title: Observe a tagged installed workflow and read E2E proof in Intent

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: tagged and working-tree prepared origins never share a cache identity

**Verdict: Confirmed missing test path** (bounded to the examined checks below).

**Story and revision.** SEED-334#observe-tagged-install-and-read-e2e-proof, plan .planning/slice-plans/891-observe-tagged-install-and-read-e2e-proof/PLAN.md, completed revision fda707f32f03b027d91fdfd04dbe5f3ceb3ea667, checked out in a detached scratch worktree at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/3ec66d8d/tmp/ic-scratch with its own `npm ci` (Node 24.21.0). The worktree was clean before the probe and has been removed since.

**Promise.** A working-tree preparation journey never receives the tagged v0.3.97 prepared origin, and the tagged journey never receives the working-tree origin.

**Fault.** In dashboard/test-support/support/startOriginPreparation.ts, `startOriginArtifactKey`:
`const suffix = release === undefined ? "" : \`-release-${release.tag}\`;` was changed to `const suffix = "";`.
With this change, `startOriginArtifacts()` registers `start-origin-codex-queued` twice. The global setup builds a `new Map([...])` (e2eGlobalSetup.ts and backendGlobalSetup.ts), so the later released entry replaces the working-tree one. Every Codex queued journey then resolves the v0.3.97 origin. No fixtures or assertions were changed. A shell `trap` restored the file.

**Maintained checks examined (the caller's command, unchanged; the runner's strict reporter; proof records read with OPEN_DOUGH_*_PROOF_RECORD).**
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e -- launches/released-installation-preparation.spec.ts launches/agent-launch-preparation- --workers=1` selected 7 tests: agent-launch-preparation-codex-recovery, -codex-retry, -codex, -cursor, -kept, -phases, and released-installation-preparation.
- Backend: `npm run test:dashboard:backend -- dashboard/backend-tests/launches/start-origin-isolation.spec.ts dashboard/backend-tests/launches/released-installation-tag.spec.ts` ran 4 tests: the 3 start-origin-isolation tests and the pinned-tag-unavailable test.

**Independent scratch witness (untracked, removed afterwards).** e2e/launches/zz-intent-witness.spec.ts used the same `preparationPage` `origin` fixture with `preparationHost: "codex"` and no release. That is the fixture path the agent-launch-preparation-codex* journeys use. It asserted that `<origin.project>/.agents/skills/dough-update/VERSION` is absent. That file comes only from the released installer; the working-tree installation installs just the five start skills. The witness ran with the e2e selection above, for 8 tests in total.

**Run observations.**
- Baseline: e2e 8/8 expected, exit 0. Backend 4/4 expected, exit 0. This passing baseline exercised every selected check.
- Faulted: the witness failed (`expect(existsSync(version)).toBe(false)`, received `true`). A working-tree Codex preparation origin held the released v0.3.97 installation. That is the independently observed wrong behavior on the intended path. All 7 maintained e2e journeys still passed, including the 4 working-tree Codex journeys that receive the same fixture origin. All 4 backend tests passed, including "concurrent installed starts…", which itself requests `startOriginArtifactKey("codex", "queued")` and so received the released origin.
- Restored: `git diff` was empty and the only untracked file was the witness. E2E was 8/8 expected and backend 4/4 expected, both exit 0. The witness was then deleted, and the worktree was removed with `git worktree remove`.

**Finding.** The examined maintained proof does not catch a working-tree journey receiving the tagged origin. The working-tree journeys and start-origin-isolation pass whichever installation they receive. released-installation-preparation checks the released provenance (tag, revision, VERSION, command) only on the tagged journey, and under this fault that journey still receives the release. The omitted transition is a working-tree preparation journey (or `requestRunArtifact(startOriginArtifactKey(layout, runWide))`) that checks its origin carries the working-tree installation and not the released one. The reverse case, a tagged journey receiving the working-tree origin, would be caught by released-installation-preparation's provenance `toEqual`, because a working-tree origin has no dough-update/VERSION. That reverse case was not run here.
This probe did not exercise the parallel `privateKey` tag component (private, per-process origins). The examined checks have no assertion that would distinguish it either, so it is likely the same gap, but this is unverified.

**Next proof action.** Add one assertion that a working-tree prepared origin (for example, the Codex queued run artifact a working-tree preparation journey starts from) holds no released installation, such as no `dough-update/VERSION` or the working-tree marker as in "successive preparations install current working-tree source…". Place it beside start-origin-isolation or in a working-tree Codex preparation journey, so the shared-key collision fails it. The scratch witness above is one minimal form.

**Prior disposition.** None known. Only the forward fault (empty override → ENOENT) had been observed. This is a new gap, and the repair decision stays with the caller.

**Secondary (report only, no break run).** Slice 3 added `"**/*Cases.ts"` to the e2e location's include list in .planning/open-dough.json (line 16). A grep of dashboard/, e2e/, scripts/ and Distribution/tests found no test that references that include pattern or asserts that e2e `*Cases.ts` helpers are selected. The `*Cases.ts` hits are only helper imports (for example, styledDiffCases.ts and authenticatedReadRefusalCases.ts). By inspection, the include looks unprotected. Without a faulted observation this is not a verdict.

**Side observation.** After the probe, the execution checkout showed `M .planning/slice-plans/586-launch-test-intent/PLAN.md` and `M .planning/slice-plans/617-keep-one-browser-test-group-roster/PLAN.md`. This probe never touched the execution checkout's tracked files, so these edits likely come from another session. They were left as found.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** Measured wall-clock seconds per command, from shell `date`: e2e baseline 37 s (no proof record) and 54 s (with proof record), faulted 35 s, restored 42 s. Backend baseline 7 s and 5 s, faulted 11 s, restored 7 s. There was also one 48 s e2e run that failed only on the witness's console output under the strict reporter; it was fixed and rerun. The e2e total is about 216 s and the backend total about 30 s. Load averages were about 8 to 11 during the runs.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: the agent ran the probe without human interaction, and no human time was measured.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no separately supported token or turn measure is exposed to this agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 377310 ms (measured), from 1795832778443 to 1795833155753 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision: fda707f32f03b027d91fdfd04dbe5f3ceb3ea667. Verdict: Confirmed missing test path for "tagged and working-tree prepared origins never share a cache identity" (working-tree journey given the tagged origin). Evidence: the key-suffix fault in `startOriginArtifactKey` passed every maintained check and failed only the scratch witness. Decision: no delivered defect (scratch fault only); routine test strengthening queued last as correction [SEED-334#prove-working-tree-origins-hold-no-release](seeds/SEED-334-product-wide-end-to-end-tests.md#prove-working-tree-origins-hold-no-release) (plan 894), which also notes the unverified `privateKey` gap. Secondary: the slice 3 `**/*Cases.ts` include has no maintained check; no break run, no follow-up — its outcome is observed on the production dashboard after integration.
